title: Nonstationary Load Pacer with Boundary-Aware Sampler and Quantile Drift Reporter
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Current benchmark runners assume stationary arrival processes (Poisson / constant QPS) which under-represent real production patterns (startup ramps, diurnal drift, heavy-tailed burst windows, and sporadic degradations). This PR introduces a configurable nonstationary load pacer plus a boundary-aware sampler to ensure representative tail coverage, and a compact quantile-drift reporter for automated regression detection.

What this changes: - New pacer module (bench/pacers/nonstationary_pacer.py) that synthesizes time-varying arrival rates via piecewise-defined functions (ramps, sinusoids, burst impulses, step changes) and supports a user-specified schedule file. The pacer exposes deterministic seeds, repeatable epoching, and optional jitter models to exercise scheduler jitter in the runtime. - Boundary-aware sampler (bench/samplers/boundary_sampler.py) which prioritizes generating traces that hit sequence-length boundaries, KV cache cold boundaries, and precise token-offset windows. It implements adaptive oversampling for rare boundary events while keeping global QPS budget intact. - Quantile drift reporter (bench/reporters/quantile_drift_reporter.py) that collects sliding-window quantiles (p50/p90/p95/p99) per-cohort and emits a compact drift histogram plus a CSV/JSON payload suitable for downstream aggregation. The reporter computes Wasserstein distance and an asymmetric drift score to prioritize regressions that affect tails more than medians. - Integration harness updates: runner config schema extended (bench/configs/nonstationary_examples.yaml), CI workload profile (ci/bench_profiles/ci_nonstationary.yaml) and a lightweight end-to-end integration test that runs a 30s diurnal+burst scenario on a small local runner to validate determinism.

Checklist: - [x] Core pacer implementation with API and unit tests - [x] Sampler implementation with focused unit tests for boundary coverage - [x] Quantile drift reporter with unit tests and example outputs - [x] Integration test + CI profile - [x] Docs: short README with usage examples and config reference

Compatibility notes: The pacer is additive — existing stationary profiles remain supported. Default behavior without a schedule file is backward-compatible (falls back to constant QPS). No runtime API changes to serving binaries; all changes live in the benchmark-lab harness.

Performance notes: On local CI profile (30s diurnal + burst) the end-to-end harness added ~0.8s of overhead per 60s window due to extra sampling bookkeeping; this is acceptable for offline benchmark runs and the reporter is low-overhead (sub-1% CPU in our microbench runs).

Related work: ENG-4123 (represent real-world arrival patterns), ENG-4189 (improve tail coverage), SUP-2241 (support ticket requesting diurnal scenario for a customer incident).

How to run: see bench/README.md -> Section "Nonstationary pacer" for a full invocation; quick start: python -m bench.runner --profile ci_nonstationary.yaml --seed 42.

Notes on determinism and seeding: The pacer accepts a global seed that deterministically generates the schedule + jitter stream. The integration test asserts byte-for-byte identical sequence IDs and timestamp offsets when run with the same seed and host time zone.

Risks and follow-ups: - We added more knobs which can be misused; documented recommended presets for CI vs. long-running fidelity tests. - Follow-ups: add a Flink-based aggregator for large-scale runs (ENG-4216).

review_comments: Evan Park (reviewer): Can we guarantee determinism across platforms? timezone / clock differences have bitten us before.

Maya Chen (author): The pacer uses monotonic offsets and serializes event timestamps relative to epoch-0 in the harness; we added a deterministic timezone-agnostic checkpoint in the integration test. See test_nonstationary_pacer.py for the assertion.
Diego Valdez (reviewer): Metric names look fine but please use canonical prefix bench.quantile_drift.* to avoid collisions with runtime metrics.
Maya Chen (author): Updated metric prefix and added a small mapping function in reporter; pushed fix (de4f219).
Ruth Almeida (reviewer): The oversampling factor could blow up overall token budget if misconfigured — can we cap it?
Maya Chen (author): Added a configurable max_oversample parameter and a hard cap in the sampler to ensure global QPS budget is respected. Added tests verifying the cap behaviour.
ci_checks: integration: pass (ci_nonstationary profile on small runner)
release_notes: Add nonstationary load pacer and boundary-aware sampler to benchmark-lab; include quantile drift reporter and CI profile for nonstationary scenarios. Backwards compatible with existing profiles.
notes: This PR is intended to improve fidelity of performance baselines by simulating realistic nonstationary traffic and ensuring regressions in tails are visible in automated drift reports.
